source_text:
Δευτέρα δὲ ἐντολὴ τῆς διδαχῆς:
οὐ φονεύσεις, οὐ μοιχεύσεις, οὐ παιδοφθορήσεις, οὐ πορνεύσεις, οὐ κλέψεις, οὐ μαγεύσεις, οὐ φαρμακεύσεις, οὐ φονεύσεις τέκνον ἐν φθορᾷ, οὐδὲ γεννηθὲν ἀποκτενεῖς, οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις τὰ τοῦ πλησίον.
οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, οὐ ψευδομαρτυρήσεις, οὐ κακολογήσεις, οὐ μνησικακήσεις.
οὐκ ἔσῃ διγνώμων οὐδὲ δίγλωσσος: παγὶς γὰρ θανάτου ἡ διγλωσσία.
οὐκ ἔσται ὁ λόγος σου ψευδής, οὐ κενός, ἀλλὰ μεμεστωμένος πράξει,
οὐκ ἔσῃ πλεονέκτης οὐδὲ ἅρπαξ οὐδὲ ὑποκριτὴς οὐδὲ κακοήθης οὐδὲ ὑπερήφανος. οὐ λήψῃ βουλὴν πονηρὰν κατὰ τοῦ πλησίον σου.
οὐ μισήσεις πάντα ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ οὓς μὲν ἐλέγξεις, περὶ δὲ ὦν προσεύξῃ, οὓς δὲ ἀγαπήσεις ὑπὲρ τὴν ψυχήν σου.
thought_title: The Second Commandment of the Teaching
orientation: The anonymous teacher continues the Two Ways instruction, now listing the prohibitions of the second commandment of the teaching.
pass_a_gloss: A second [now] commandment of the teaching: You will not murder, you will not commit adultery, you will not sexually corrupt a child, you will not commit fornication, you will not steal, you will not practice magic or sorcery, you will not murder a child in corruption, nor [one] born will you kill, you will not desire the [things] of the neighbor. You will not swear falsely, you will not bear false witness, you will not speak evil, you will not bear a grudge. You will not be double-minded nor double-tongued: for a snare of death [is] the double-tonguedness. Your word will not be false, [nor] empty, but filled with action. You will not be greedy nor a robber nor a hypocrite nor malicious nor arrogant. You will not take a wicked plan against your neighbor. You will not hate every man, but some [indeed] you will reprove, and concerning some you will pray, and some you will love above your soul.

choices.why: The verb means to sexually violate or corrupt a child; 'corrupt a child' keeps the literal force without modernizing to a specific legal term.
The verb refers to the use of drugs or potions for magical purposes; 'practice sorcery' distinguishes it from μαγεύσεις, rendered 'practice magic'.
The phrase likely refers to abortion or destruction in the womb; 'in corruption' preserves the literal wording without resolving the debated sense.
The compound means having two minds or divided judgment; 'double-minded' is the standard literal rendering.
The compound means speaking with two tongues, i.e., saying different things to different people; 'double-tongued' keeps the metaphor.
The phrase means loving some people more than one's own life; 'above your soul' preserves the literal wording and the Semitic sense of ψυχή as life.

bible_refs.note: οὐ φονεύσεις, οὐ μοιχεύσεις, οὐ κλέψεις

pass_b_english: The second commandment of the teaching is this: You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not sexually corrupt a child, you shall not commit sexual immorality, you shall not steal, you shall not practice magic or sorcery, you shall not kill a child by abortion, nor kill one that has been born, and you shall not covet what belongs to your neighbor.
You shall not swear falsely, you shall not bear false witness, you shall not speak evil, and you shall not bear a grudge.
Do not be double-minded or double-tongued, for double-tonguedness is a snare of death.
Your word must not be false or empty, but filled with action.
Do not be greedy, or a robber, or a hypocrite, or malicious, or arrogant. Do not take evil counsel against your neighbor.
Do not hate anyone. Instead, some you shall correct, for others you shall pray, and some you shall love above your own soul.

problems.why: περὶ ὦν means 'for whom' or 'concerning whom'; 'for some' changes the relative construction and loses 'concerning'

problems.quote: you shall not murder a child in corruption
problems.why: ἐν φθορᾷ means 'by abortion' or 'in the womb'; 'in corruption' misreads φθορά
problems.fix: you shall not kill a child by abortion
problems.ruling: ἐν φθορᾷ here means 'by abortion'; 'in corruption' misleads readers about the act described.

edits.old: you shall not murder a child in corruption
edits.new: you shall not kill a child by abortion

problems.why: Fleshly/bodily desires and sexual immorality overlap but are distinct concepts; reader may conflate them.
problems.fix: Keep distinct: fleshly desires = broader term; sexual immorality = specific sin.

problems.quote: you shall not corrupt a child
problems.why: 'Corrupt a child' and 'corrupters of God's formed work' may refer to same sin (pederasty/abortion) but reader cannot tell.
problems.fix: Add footnote linking the two expressions or clarify the referent.

variants.text: you shall not corrupt a child

problems.quote: you shall not practice magic, you shall not practice sorcery
problems.why: Magic/sorcery rendered with varying noun and verb forms across sections; reader may miss they are the same category.
problems.fix: Use consistent English for the same Greek term across sections.

variants.text: you shall not practice magic, you shall not practice sorcery

edits.old: you shall not corrupt a child
edits.new: you shall not sexually corrupt a child

edits.old: you shall not practice magic, you shall not practice sorcery
edits.new: you shall not practice magic or sorcery

fixed: The English already says exactly what the source says for the first problem; no edit needed.
The English already says exactly what the source says for the second problem; no edit needed.
The English already says exactly what the source says for the third problem; no edit needed.

last_rejected.quote: nor kill one that has been born
last_rejected.why: ἀποκτενεῖς is future indicative 'you shall kill,' not 'you shall not kill'—negation already in οὐδέ.
last_rejected.fix: nor shall you kill one that has been born
last_rejected.ruling: οὐδέ + future indicative functions as prohibition; 'nor kill' correctly renders οὐδὲ ἀποκτενεῖς.

last_rejected.why: ἔσῃ is future indicative 'you shall be,' not imperative/subjunctive 'do not be'—negation already in οὐκ.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐκ ἔσῃ is negative future functioning as prohibition; 'Do not be' correctly renders it.

last_rejected.quote: Your word must not be false or empty
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἔσται ὁ λόγος σου ψευδής, οὐ κενός
last_rejected.why: ἔσται is future indicative 'shall not be,' not 'must not be'—changes modality from command to necessity.
last_rejected.fix: Your word shall not be false or empty
last_rejected.ruling: 'must not be' preserves prohibitive force of οὐκ ἔσται; modality shift is negligible.

last_rejected.why: ἔσῃ is future indicative 'you shall be,' not imperative 'do not be'—negation already in οὐκ.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐκ ἔσῃ is negative future as prohibition; 'Do not be' correctly renders it.

last_rejected.why: λήψῃ is future indicative 'you shall take,' not imperative 'do not take'—negation already in οὐ.
last_rejected.fix: You shall not take evil counsel
last_rejected.ruling: οὐ λήψῃ is negative future as prohibition; 'Do not take' correctly renders it.

last_rejected.why: μισήσεις is future indicative 'you shall hate,' not imperative 'do not hate'—negation already in οὐ.
last_rejected.fix: You shall not hate any person
last_rejected.ruling: οὐ μισήσεις is negative future as prohibition; 'Do not hate' correctly renders it.
